card.hook: Here's a fun one: open water at your feet and a whole mountainside stacked up behind it, and you barely have to try. Zauchensee gives you that postcard shot almost for free.
card.stand_here: Stand on Alte Zauchenseestraße, about 536 metres north of the lake, and face south. The water and the mountain slopes are straight ahead of you. Want a closer look? Just stroll on towards the shore.
card.zoom: Start at 0.5x to squeeze the lake and slopes into one shot, then switch to 1x for a more natural view. Try 2x or 5x (depending on your phone) to pick out a far bit of shoreline or a ridge.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines and put the horizon on the top or bottom third line, then tap the mountains and slide it a little darker if the sky looks washed out.
card.best_time: Early morning or late afternoon usually gives softer light than midday. You're shooting south, so check which way the light falls on the day.
card.selfie_here: Flip to the front camera, switch to 0.5x if your phone has it, and hold it a bit above eye level. Turn so the lake and slopes sit behind your shoulder and you're all in the frame.
card.rules_and_safety: This is a resort area, so check the official site before you go for any local access rules or restrictions near the shore.
card.challenge: Find a spot where a ski lift or slope peeks into your shot, then try to catch the slopes reflected in the water too.
card.good_to_know: The lake sits at about 1,339 metres, the lowest point of an area that climbs to the Steinfeldspitze at 2,344 metres. That height difference is why the view works so well. The resort grew from the 1960s, when the first T-bar started running in the winter of 1964/65, and it has hosted Alpine Ski World Cup races many times since 1980.

selfie_research.notes: No page I found names a selfie or photo spot with Zauchensee lake behind the visitor, so I did not add one. The only lake-side places named were the Seewand Klettersteig (via ferrata) starting from the parking area directly at the lake, and a viewpoint on that route. Those sources describe a climbing route with exposed sections, which makes it unsuitable as an everyday selfie spot, so I left it out. The Rosskopf photo point found in the Ski amadé guide is a mountain viewpoint, not a lakeside spot. A forum post mentions a photo point in Zauchensee that uses a lift pass, but its location is unclear. No page gave a spot where a passer-by could photograph a visitor with the whole lake in frame. No selfie-stick or tripod rules were stated on any page I read.

card.hook: Nobody walks up to this start. It's so steep that you ride the Weltcupexpress railway instead, and the view when you step out explains why.
card.stand_here: Stand right at the subject: the Gamskogel viewing platform at the women's World Cup start. Face down the slope, and the Kälberloch section sits below you.
card.zoom: Start at 0.5x to catch the whole drop and the sweep of the mountain. Then try 1x for a balanced look down the piste, and 2x or 5x (depending on your phone) to pick out the Kälberloch section below.
card.make_it_pop: Snow can turn grey in photos, so tap a bright patch of the slope and slide the brightness up a little.
card.best_time: Pick a clear day so you can see all the way down the course. Mornings are usually calmer, but any bright, clear spell works, and check the railway times first.
card.selfie_here: Hold your phone at arm's length with the front camera, switch to 0.5x if your phone has it, and let the long slope fall away behind your shoulder. Take a couple of frames so you can pick the one where you aren't squinting at the snow.
card.rules_and_safety: Stay well behind the barriers and don't lean out for a better angle, because the ground falls away sharply. The Weltcupexpress is seasonal and may charge a ticket, so check opening times locally.
card.challenge: Turn on the gridlines and run the piste diagonally through the frame. Can you make it look as steep as it feels?
card.good_to_know: Kälberloch first hosted racing in 1990 and is regarded as the most demanding course on the women's World Cup circuit. The full women's downhill is just over 3 km long, with a drop of nearly 800 m from a start at about 2,176 m. For a second angle, the terrace of the Unterbergalm hut looks across the race slope as it runs through the snow bowl.

selfie_research.notes: No page I found names a selfie spot with Kälberloch behind it, or a spot where a passer-by should stand to photograph a visitor with the whole landmark, so I have not proposed any. Kälberloch is a section of the Zauchensee women's World Cup downhill course on the Gamskogel, not a standalone landmark (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%A4lberloch; https://www.zauchensee.at/en/race-track/world-cup-course-zauchensee.html). The nearest viewpoint with a named page is the Gamskogel course start, reached by the Weltcup-Express at 2,176 m, which the page describes as a fine viewpoint (https://www.meinbezirk.at/lungau/c-reisen/aussichtspunkt-gamskogel-start-der-weltcupstrecke_a155109). That page does not say the Kälberloch is visible behind a photo spot, so I left it out. The Unterbergalm hut sits in the middle of the Kälberloch course and has a large terrace (https://www.felseralm-zauchensee.at/die-huette-unterbergalm-zauchensee-salzburg.html), but no page links it to a photo spot, so it is also not proposed. No rules on selfie sticks or tripods and no safety point were found on the pages I read. A visitor could check the course or the Gamskogel start on site before relying on any photo spot.

card.hook: Sometimes the best photo is the simple one: a mountain hut, a big sky and nobody asking you to be clever. Felserhütte is that kind of spot, and you can be in position in about a minute.
card.stand_here: Head for the phone icon near Zauchenseestraße, about 15 m south of the hut. Face north and the hut will be right in front of you.
card.zoom: Start at 1x for a natural view of the hut and its surroundings. If you can't squeeze the whole building in, tap 0.5x. Then try 2x or 5x for details like the roof or windows (higher zooms depend on your phone).
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines and put the hut on one of the lower intersections, leaving open space above for sky or mountainside.
card.best_time: Morning or late afternoon gives softer light and gentler shadows on the walls than the middle of the day. Check the sky before you go, because clear weather shows off the hut's surroundings best.
card.selfie_here: Use the front camera and tap 0.5x so the hut fits in behind you. Stand with the hut over your shoulder and hold the phone a little higher than your face.
card.rules_and_safety: The hut may be private or in commercial use, so check the official site or local signs before you go and stay on public paths. If people are nearby, don't block paths or doors.
card.challenge: Take one shot standing and one slightly crouched, then see which has the cleaner background.
card.good_to_know: Felserhütte is in the Zauchensee area, a mountain resort in the Austrian Alps. The roof lines, walls and landscape make an easy scene that reads well even on a small screen. If people, vehicles or signs creep in at the edges, step a pace to either side.

selfie_research.notes: No page I found names a selfie spot with the Felserhütte behind the visitor, or a spot where a passer-by should stand to photograph a visitor with the whole hut, so both fields are empty. The closest leads were not usable: the hut's sun terrace is named on the hut's own gallery (https://felseralm-zauchensee.at/bildergalerie-felserhuette-zauchensee-salzburg.html) and on zauchenseehof.com (https://www.zauchenseehof.com/en/on-the-slopes), but no page calls it a photo spot. Skiresort.info lists a 'Felserhütte in Zauchensee near Zauchi's Kinderland' photo (https://www.skiresort.info/ski-resort/zauchensee-flachauwinkl/photos/), but that is a caption with no description of the viewpoint. The ski area has 'photo points' and 'love hearts' (https://www.zauchensee.at/en/winter/skiparadise-zauchensee-flachauwinkl.html), but no page places them relative to the hut. The address is also inconsistent across sources: 'Zauchensee 21' on snooop.net and felseralm-zauchensee.at, 'Hauptstrasse' on restauranttester.at. A local check on the ground would be needed before adding any spot.

card.hook: Here's the secret of Garnhofalm: you don't get close, and that's the point. From the map spot the hut is a small building sitting in a big, wide mountain scene, and that's the picture you're after.
card.stand_here: Stand at the phone icon on Alte Zauchenseestraße, about 530 m north of the subject, and face south. Garnhofalm is the building out in front of you.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x to catch the foreground, the slopes and the sky in one shot. Then try zoom 2x or 5x (depending on your phone) to bring the building closer without walking an inch.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on your gridlines, put the building on one of the lines, then tap the building and slide a bit darker if the sky looks washed out.
card.best_time: Soft morning or late-afternoon light usually flatters mountain scenery. Check the weather and daylight on the day.
card.selfie_here: Head to the wooden jetty (Steg) on the Zauchensee lake shore, where the mountain panorama sits behind you. Use the front camera, try zoom 0.5x, and hold the phone a little low so the peaks fit over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Ask someone at the edge of Zauchi's Kinderland, the children's ski area, to take your photo, and stand so the hut is in view behind you.
card.rules_and_safety: Access to the hut and the land around it may be limited, so check the official site before you go and respect any signs or fences.
card.challenge: Take one wide shot where the hut is just a tiny dot in the scenery, then one closer shot. Which one would you frame on your wall?
card.good_to_know: Garnhofalm appears to be the same place as the Garnhofhütte, at about 1350 m. The map spot is roughly 6 to 7 minutes on foot from the hut if you fancy a closer look, though the route may vary. Stick to signed paths.

selfie_spots.name: Steg am See (lakeside jetty), Zauchensee
selfie_spots.detail: on the wooden jetty (Steg) at the Zauchensee lake shore, with the mountain panorama behind
selfie_spots.why: A wedding photo on the hut's listing shows this jetty framed by the mountain lake and peaks, which is the best-documented photo setting near the hut.

ask_someone_spot.name: Zauchi's Kinderland (Übungslift Kinderland), Zauchensee ski area
ask_someone_spot.detail: in the children's ski area Kinderland, where a published photo of the Garnhofhütte was taken; stand at the edge of the area so the hut is in view

selfie_research.notes: Garnhofalm appears to be the same place as the Garnhofhütte (GaHü), Zauchensee 23 / Palfen 72, 5541 Altenmarkt-Zauchensee, at about 1350 m; the listed coordinates match your position. No page names a selfie spot with the hut itself as the backdrop, so the jetty spot is inferred from a wedding photo caption and should be checked on the ground. The ask-someone spot is only a general area named by skiresort.info, not an exact standing point. No page I found states rules on selfie sticks or tripods, and no safety point was stated. The Rosskopf photo point is a different location from the hut, so I left it out.
